# GPU metric catalog v1.7.0

Canonical catalog of the GPU and control-plane signals KubeNeuron recognises. It describes signals only: no alert rule, detector threshold, playbook or controller behaviour is derived from it.

Every DCGM entry has a **source side** (the DCGM field id and name, the legacy names the id has carried, the series the pinned dcgm-exporter uses, whether the shipped profile lists it, the raw unit) and a **canonical side** (the `kubeneuron_gpu_*` series it feeds, the canonical unit and factor, and the fixed labels that merge several DCGM fields into one canonical metric).

> **Contract, not inventory.** A canonical mapping is the contract the shipped recording rules implement: it states the kubeneuron_gpu_* series, unit and fixed labels the rules derive from the source field. Since v1.6.0 the canonical recording rules (configs/vmalert/gpu-recording-rules.yaml, mirrored in the deployed VMRule) record every mapped series from its source series, so a canonical series exists exactly when its source series is scraped; an absent source yields no canonical sample, never a synthesised zero. A recorded series is not a validated one: the rules add no hardware evidence, and every support cell stands as the catalog states it. The source side is likewise a description: a DCGM field is emitted by the pinned dcgm-exporter only when the shipped profile lists its series (profiled = yes, source = dcgm-exporter); every other DCGM field has source = dcgm-field, which means it is cataloged by id from NVIDIA documentation and no exporter is asserted to emit it.

Tiers have fixed meanings: **T0** baseline GPU telemetry, **T1** GPU reliability telemetry, **T2** DCGM effective-work / profiling telemetry (deferred, no entries), **T3** serving / Triton telemetry (deferred, no entries), **T4** KubeNeuron control-plane telemetry. Tier T4 is the control plane and is unrelated to the Tesla T4 GPU, which is a hardware column. Hardware support is a separate dimension; `validated` means a recorded run of this project observed the value, and every such cell cites its evidence; `not-applicable` is asserted only where NVIDIA documentation establishes the feature is absent, otherwise a cell is `unknown`. No v0.7 hardware validation has been performed; `declared` cells are unvalidated.

Units: `raw` is what the source emits; `canonical` is the normalised unit with `canonical = raw × factor` (a decode, marked `decoded`, has no factor). `Profiled` is `yes` only when the shipped exporter profile (deploy/kubernetes/dependencies/gpu-operator/values.yaml) lists the source series, so the pinned exporter is configured to emit it; every other field is cataloged from NVIDIA documentation and no exporter is asserted to emit it. `Source` says the same thing as a value: `dcgm-exporter` exactly for the profiled fields, `dcgm-field` for a field that is merely cataloged. `Source series` is the name the exporter uses for the id when it does emit it, which is the legacy DCGM name where DCGM renamed the field; the current DCGM name is accepted as an alias on exporter builds that know it. A cataloged-only entry is marked deferred and is enabled in no profile, read by no rule and attached to no action.

## Canonical series (recording-rule contract)

One row per `kubeneuron_gpu_*` series, with every DCGM field that feeds it and the fixed labels that keep the rows apart. `Profiled sources` names the feeding fields the shipped exporter profile lists today (source `dcgm-exporter`); a series whose sources are all unprofiled (source `dcgm-field`) has no input until the profile changes. The recording rules in `configs/vmalert/gpu-recording-rules.yaml` (mirrored in the deployed VMRule) record every series below from its profiled sources with the stated factor and labels; a series exists exactly when a source is scraped, and recording it is not evidence that any hardware reports the source. The derived signals below read these series. The only alerts that read any of them are the shadow-only ShadowGpu* rules (`configs/vmalert/gpu-shadow-rules.yaml`), which route to humans and trigger no remediation; no controller-facing alert reads a canonical series.

## Derived signals

Series the `gpu-derived-*` recording groups in `configs/vmalert/gpu-recording-rules.yaml` (mirrored in the deployed VMRule) compute from canonical series, Tier T4 control-plane series or derived series declared earlier in this table. `Formula` is the rule expression verbatim; `Inputs` are the canonical series, Tier T4 control-plane series or earlier derived series it reads, and nothing reads a dcgm-exporter series directly. `No data` states what an absent sample means: no formula uses `or vector(0)`, `default` or `absent()`, so a derived series is missing when an input its formula needs at that instant is missing or a divisor guard (`> 0`) excludes the sample, never replaced by a fabricated zero. Which inputs a formula needs is stated per row: most rows need every input, while the thermal headroom needs either the margin or both fallback inputs (slowdown threshold and temperature) and is missing only when neither is reported. `Carried` labels flow through from the input; fixed labels are added by the rule. Each series is one component: there is deliberately no aggregate health or error score, because one number would hide which component moved. The only score in the table is the experimental fail-slow peer score, which compares one device to its peers and sums no components. A row may read a derived series declared above it (the fail-slow score reads the clock and throttle ratios); table order is evaluation order. Rows marked experimental are shadow signals whose formula may change: they are read only by the Fail-slow Radar board and the shadow-only ShadowGpuFailSlow alert, which triggers no remediation, and by no controller path. Recording a derived series is not evidence that any hardware reports its inputs.

| `kubeneuron_gpu_thermal_headroom_celsius` | gauge | celsius | — | — | `gpu-derived-thermal` | `kubeneuron_gpu_thermal_margin_celsius`, `kubeneuron_gpu_temperature_limit_celsius`, `kubeneuron_gpu_temperature_celsius` | `kubeneuron_gpu_thermal_margin_celsius or (label_del(kubeneuron_gpu_temperature_limit_celsius{limit="slowdown"}, "limit") - kubeneuron_gpu_temperature_celsius)` | absent when the GPU reports neither a thermal margin (153) nor both a slowdown threshold (158) and a temperature (150); the fallback is used only for devices with no margin sample, never summed with it. | Degrees of headroom before thermal slowdown: the reported thermal margin, else slowdown threshold minus GPU temperature. |

| `kubeneuron_gpu_fail_slow_score_ratio` | gauge | ratio | — | — | `gpu-derived-fail-slow` | `kubeneuron_gpu_clock_ratio`, `kubeneuron_gpu_throttle_share_ratio` | `(1 - max by (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) (kubeneuron_gpu_clock_ratio{domain="sm"}) / on (gpu_model) group_left() (median by (gpu_model) (max by (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) (kubeneuron_gpu_clock_ratio{domain="sm"})) > 0)) >= 0.15 and on (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) (max by (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) (kubeneuron_gpu_throttle_share_ratio) >= 0.05) and on (gpu_model) (count by (gpu_model) (max by (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) (kubeneuron_gpu_clock_ratio{domain="sm"})) >= 3)` | shadow only: read by the Fail-slow Radar board and the shadow-only ShadowGpuFailSlow alert, which route to humans and trigger no remediation; no controller path consumes it. Absent unless all three gates hold at the sample instant: score = 1 - own SM clock ratio / median SM clock ratio of the gpu_model peer group is at least 0.15 (own clock at least 15% below the peer median); the device's maximum throttle share over 5m across reasons is at least 0.05; and the gpu_model has at least 3 distinct devices (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) reporting an SM clock ratio. Inputs are deduplicated to (node, gpu_uuid, gpu_model) before the median and the count, so pod, namespace and container labels do not appear on the result and cannot weight the peer group. Also absent when the peer median is 0 or either input is missing. A healthy, idle or singleton device has no sample, not 0. | Fail-slow degradation score: how far the SM clock ratio sits below its gpu_model peer median (1 - own/peer_median), recorded only when the device is also throttled and has at least 3 peers. Experimental: the formula may change before anything relies on it. |

### Derived signals intentionally not recorded

These series are No data by design: no rule records them, and the reason is stated so the gap is not mistaken for a missing rule.

- `kubeneuron_gpu_present` (gauge, boolean): 1 while the node advertises the GPU as allocatable. Not recorded. intentionally No data: a presence signal needs the node's allocatable nvidia.com/gpu from kube-state-metrics, which is not an established dependency of this project. Until it is, there is no honest source for a GPU that exists but reports nothing, and no rule records this series.

### DCGM fields with no canonical series

- 190 `DCGM_FI_DEV_PSTATE`: not a row of Appendix A; no canonical series is assigned until a dashboard or rule needs the P-state.
- 230 `DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS`: a sticky last-value gauge cannot feed kubeneuron_gpu_xid_errors_total: a rate over it sees no repeats and keeps the last code forever. The counter is reserved until an event-counter source (DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_TOTAL or a kernel-log watcher) is cataloged; see reserved_canonical.
- 1523 `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_RECOVERY_ACTION`: cataloged only; kubeneuron_gpu_recovery_action is reserved until the field is enabled and its value enumeration is cataloged; see reserved_canonical.

### Reserved canonical names

Names the brief defines that no cataloged source may claim yet. The validator rejects any mapping to them.

- `kubeneuron_gpu_xid_errors_total`: needs an event counter source: DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_TOTAL once confirmed to label each XID code, or a kernel-log (kmsg) watcher. DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS (230) keeps only the last code for the hostengine's lifetime, so a repeat is invisible and a rate over it would count nothing or count one event forever. The gauge therefore maps to no canonical series; this counter stays reserved until a counter source is cataloged.
- `kubeneuron_gpu_recovery_action`: DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_RECOVERY_ACTION (1523) is cataloged only: not enabled in any profile, not shown to be exposed by the pinned dcgm-exporter, unvalidated on every hardware and attached to no action. A canonical series for it is assigned when the field is first enabled, together with the enumeration of its values.

## Evidence

- `DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS`: v0.6.0-era run, not v0.7: the agent gpuhealth source (internal/agent/gpuhealth, dcgmi dmon -e 230) read this field on the Tesla T4 stand during the hw-e2e test-dcgm phase; see the v0.6.0 section of CHANGELOG.md. The XID was injected, not a natural fault. No v0.7 validation has been performed.

## Shipped consumers

Files and components whose expressions or code read the source series today. This is a claim independent of `Profiled`: the exporter profile (deploy/kubernetes/dependencies/gpu-operator/values.yaml) is never listed here, and a profiled series with no reader is a legitimate state (the profile can list a series before any rule reads it). Since v1.6.0 every profiled series is read by the canonical recording rules (`configs/vmalert/gpu-recording-rules.yaml`, mirrored in `deploy/kubernetes/dependencies/observability/rules.yaml`); only the nine v0.6.1 series are also read by the legacy raw alerts (`configs/vmalert/gpu-rules.yaml`).

## XID buckets

Bounded label values for `xid_bucket`. A bucket names the reporting subsystem, never an action.

| Bucket | Codes | Help |
|---|---|---|
| `application` | 13, 31, 43, 46 | Engine, page-fault and channel errors that are almost always a workload bug. |
| `ecc` | 48, 63, 64, 92, 94, 95 | ECC and row-remap events, correctable and uncorrectable alike. |
| `nvlink` | 74 | NVLink fabric errors. |
| `bus` | 79 | PCIe bus loss. |
| `gsp` | 119, 120 | GPU System Processor RPC timeouts and faults. |
| `other` | (all others) | Any XID not listed above. Counted, never classified. |

## Deferred

- **Tier T2: DCGM effective-work / profiling fields (DCGM_FI_PROF_*)** — require DCGM profiling support and exclusive access to hardware counters; not part of the MVP baseline. The only exception is the baseline PCIe byte-rate fields DCGM_FI_PROF_PCIE_TX_BYTES (1009) and DCGM_FI_PROF_PCIE_RX_BYTES (1010), which are link-traffic telemetry and sit in T0.
- **Tier T3: Triton / inference-serving metrics (nv_inference_*)** — come from a different exporter with per-model cardinality; they need their own catalog once a serving stack exists in a reference environment. The kubeneuron_serving_* names in Appendix A of the brief are not cataloged here.
- **vGPU fields (DCGM_FI_DEV_VGPU_*)** — no vGPU host in any validated environment; semantics differ per hypervisor.
- **MIG-instance scoping of listed fields** — the only hardware this project has run on (Tesla T4) is MIG-incapable; instance-level labels stay unvalidated until an A100/H100 run exists.
- **Recovery-action automation keyed to catalog entries** — the catalog describes signals only. Alert rules, detector thresholds, playbooks and controller behaviour are unchanged by it; wiring a field or XID bucket to an action is a separate, reviewed change. DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_RECOVERY_ACTION (1523) is cataloged for its id and semantics only: it is not enabled in any profile, not shown to be exposed by the pinned dcgm-exporter, attached to no action, and mapped to no canonical series (kubeneuron_gpu_recovery_action is reserved).
- **XID event counter (kubeneuron_gpu_xid_errors_total)** — the brief derives XID rate from a counter per code. The catalog's only XID field, DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS (230), is a sticky last-value gauge and is deliberately not mapped to that counter; the name is reserved until DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_TOTAL or a kernel-log watcher is cataloged as the source.
- **Alerts, consumers of the experimental fail-slow score, an aggregate health or error score and hardware evidence for the canonical and derived series** — the shipped recording rules (configs/vmalert/gpu-recording-rules.yaml and the deployed VMRule) normalise (gpu-canonical-* groups: each kubeneuron_gpu_* series is its source series times the catalog factor with the fixed labels, produced when the source exists and absent otherwise) and derive (gpu-derived-* groups: headroom, ratios, rates and hard-fault components computed from canonical series or from derived series declared earlier in the list, listed under derived). The only alerts reading them are the shadow-only ShadowGpu* rules (configs/vmalert/gpu-shadow-rules.yaml), which route to humans and trigger no remediation; the experimental fail-slow score (kubeneuron_gpu_fail_slow_score_ratio) is recorded from the derived ratios and read only by the Fail-slow Radar board and the shadow-only ShadowGpuFailSlow alert; no aggregate health or error score is defined because one number would hide which component moved, and recording a series validates nothing: every support cell stands as declared, validated (v0.6.0-era Tesla T4 evidence) or unknown exactly as before. Appendix A rows whose DCGM fields are not cataloged (NVLink byte rates 1011, 1012, which are DCGM_FI_PROF_* and tier T2; the exporter-computed DCGM_EXP_GPU_HEALTH_STATUS, which has no DCGM field id) have no mapping and no rule until their fields are added.
- **v0.7 hardware validation** — no v0.7 run has been recorded. Every validated cell cites v0.6.0-era evidence from the Tesla T4 stand; every other cell is declared from NVIDIA documentation or unknown.
